subject: maths
question:
A hollow spherical shell is made of a metal of density 21 g/cm³. Its internal and external radii are 8 cm and 9 cm, respectively. What is the weight (in kg) of the shell?

( {Use} pi = (22)/(7), {Density} = frac{{Mass}}{{Volume}} )
solution:
**Given:**

Density of the metal = 21 g/cm³

Internal radius of the hollow shell (r₁) = 8 cm

External radius of the hollow shell (r₂) = 9 cm

**Formula Used:**

Density = Mass / Volume

Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

Weight = Mass × g (where g = acceleration due to gravity = 9.8 m/s²)

**Calculation:**

Volume of the metal shell = Volume of external sphere - Volume of internal sphere

Volume of the metal shell = (4/3) × (22/7) × (9)3 - (4/3) × (22/7) × (8)3

Volume of the metal shell = (4/3) × (22/7) × [729 - 512]

Volume of the metal shell = (4/3) × (22/7) × 217

Volume of the metal shell = (4/3) × (22) × 31

Volume of the metal shell = 909.33

Mass of the shell = Density × Volume

⇒ Mass = 21 × 909.33

⇒ Mass = 19095.93 g

Convert mass to kg:

⇒ Mass = 19095.93 / 1000

⇒ Mass ≈ 19.096 kg

**The weight of the hollow spherical shell is approximately 19.096**** kg.**
